_comment: Declared intent for nova-device-doctor.sh. This file is NOT read from the
router -- the TP-Link NX620v admin UI needs an authenticated session, and
its Address Reservation table is hard-capped at 32 entries. So this is what
we believe was reserved, and the doctor checks reality against it.
Reconciling this file with the router's actual table is an agent job; see
Reservations were created 2026-08-12. They only take effect on DHCP
DISCOVER -- a router reboot does NOT migrate an existing lease, so a device
may legitimately sit on its old address until it next power-cycles.
_pre_staged: 192.168.8.107 (Lounge) was reserved while the bulb was physically
disconnected. Absence there is expected, not a fault.
_scope_comment: Only these integrations describe smart-home devices reachable by the
protocol probes this tool runs. Everything else in Home Assistant --
backup sensors, helpers, the sun -- is not a network device and must not
be graded as one. `mqtt` is included only for cloud twins published by the
Tuya bridge; Nova's own MQTT helpers are filtered out separately because
they resolve no Tuya device id.
esphome is deliberately absent: the voice satellites live there and have
their own monitoring. They are counted and named as out-of-scope rather
_expected_unavailable_comment: Unavailable right now for a known, understood reason -- unlike
retired_entities these may legitimately come back. Reported as expected so
the run stays quiet enough that a real fault stands out.

expected_unavailable_entities.light.lounge_light: LIFX bulb physically disconnected; .107 was reserved for it in advance

be graded as off-network just because a protocol probe found nothing.
